title: finite étale scheme torsor lifting
statement: Let i:Y₀ → Y be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] inducing an equivalence on finite étale schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Let M be a finite abelian group and R₀ a torsor under the constant abelian sheaf M on Y₀_et [def-sc-gm-torsor, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then there exist a scheme M-torsor t₀ over Y₀, an isomorphism of its sheaf torsor with R₀, a scheme M-torsor t over Y, and an isomorphism e:P ×_Y Y₀ ≅ P₀ over Y₀ commuting with every M-action map. A scheme M-torsor means a finite étale surjective scheme with an M-action whose map ∐_M P → P ×_Y P is an isomorphism [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor]. No connectedness, nonemptiness or surjectivity of i is assumed. The conclusion concerns geometric representatives and their actions only; no sheaf inverse-image comparison, unit equations, or arbitrary torsor transport is asserted.

proof.text: The finite constant torsor is étale locally the finite set M; hence its underlying sheaf is finite locally constant. Represent it by a finite étale scheme by Tag 03RV. Yoneda represents the constant action maps, and lifts their identities. Its sheaf torsor is isomorphic to R₀; local sections and simple transitivity make the representative a scheme torsor t₀. This is the existing EtaleTorsorDescent proof, which cannot be imported because HenselianFiniteEtale now reaches the item. Use the lower finite-locally-constant representability and Yoneda interfaces instead.
Use essential surjectivity to lift the underlying finite étale scheme. Lift its conjugated M-action maps using fullness. Faithfulness gives their zero and addition equations.

Base change preserves finite coproducts and fibre products. All their structure morphisms are finite étale, so reflect the isomorphism ∐_M P → P ×_Y P from the corresponding simple-transitivity isomorphism for t₀.

The image U of P → Y is open (étale implies flat and locally of finite presentation) and closed (finite implies proper). The clopen immersion U → Y is finite étale. Its pullback is an isomorphism since t₀ is surjective. Reflection of isomorphisms gives U=Y, hence P → Y surjective. The lifted action and comparison now give the claimed scheme torsor.
